title: fix(objectql,driver-sql): ADR-0131 8c-1 follow-up — an elevated insert whose row carries its organization warns [tenant-audit] under a wall, and a wall-exempt admin write cannot declare the exemption to the driver
body:
Filing gate **③**: a finding of the contract review of PR #25210 (record 6341425088, ③ item 3). It does not block that PR, which merged as `3a440b01f6`.
- **Who acts:** the shared queue.
- **Dedupe:** none.

Part of #15212.

## What happens on `main`
- Since #25210, the engine's isSystem `bypassTenantAudit` mute is decided by schema: a tenant column, not federated. It no longer uses a per-table ledger. About 32 platform objects with a tenant column therefore no longer have their audit muted.
- The SQL driver's `auditMissingTenant` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`, early return at about `:15999`) warns `[tenant-audit] … without options.tenantId` on create and bulkCreate as well as on update and delete. So an elevated insert whose row already carries `organization_id` warns under a walled posture. The dev's walled `os serve` printed 43 such lines at boot.
- A wall-exempt admin's REST write has no caller that can declare `bypassTenantAudit: true`: the engine sets it only for isSystem. So that line keeps firing under a wall, even though nothing needs fixing.
- **Diagnostics only:** no write changes. The ruled direction is a warning, never a silent rewrite.

## Wanted
- The insert audit is skipped when the row carries its tenant field.
- The engine declares the D8 wall-exemption to the driver, so an exempt admin's write is not told to declare an option it cannot set.
- Keep the warning's prefix byte-identical: `delivery-claim-tenant-audit.integration.test.ts` matches it.

## Acceptance
- A walled boot prints no `[tenant-audit]` line for an insert whose row carries its organization. This is pinned.
- An update or delete with no tenantId still warns. This is pinned.
- No write behaviour changes. R1–R4 hold.
